Let \(G\) be a finite group and let \(V\) be a finite \(G\)-module, viewed as an abelian normal subgroup of the semidirect product \(GV=G\ltimes V\). This work establishes upper bounds for the cardinalities of certain distinguished subsets of \(\Irr(GV)\), the set of irreducible complex characters of \(GV\).

In particular, fix an element \(v\in V\) and consider the cyclic subgroup \(\langle v\rangle\). The results bound the number of irreducible characters \(\chi\in\Irr(GV)\) for which the restricted character
\[
\chi\!\downarrow_{\langle v\rangle}
\]
is not an integer multiple of the regular character of \(\langle v\rangle\). Thus, the estimates measure how many irreducible characters fail to exhibit regular behavior when restricted to the cyclic subgroup generated by \(v\).

These bounds may provide useful tools for studying the non-coprime \(k(GV)\)-problem, where \(k(GV)=|\Irr(GV)|\) denotes the number of conjugacy classes, equivalently the number of irreducible complex characters, of the semidirect product \(GV\). In particular, controlling exceptional subsets of \(\Irr(GV)\) could contribute to a better understanding of \(k(GV)\) when the orders of \(G\) and \(V\) are not assumed to be coprime.

Let \(G\) be a finite group acting on a finite \(G\)-module \(V\), and write \(GV=G\ltimes V\) for the corresponding semidirect product. The paper studies the irreducible complex characters of \(GV\) by obtaining upper bounds for several naturally defined subsets of \(\Irr(GV)\). In particular, for a fixed element \(v\in V\), it considers those characters \(\chi\in\Irr(GV)\) whose restriction to the cyclic subgroup \(\langle v\rangle\) is not an integral multiple of the regular character of \(\langle v\rangle\). Such characters measure the failure of uniformity in the restriction of irreducible characters to subgroups generated by elements of the module.

By relating these exceptional characters to the action of \(G\) on \(V\), its orbits, and the stabilizers and centralizers of elements of \(V\), the paper develops estimates that reduce global character-counting questions to more accessible local data. The resulting bounds refine a direct estimate of the total number \(k(GV)=|\Irr(GV)|\) of conjugacy classes of the semidirect product. Since standard methods for the \(k(GV)\)-problem often depend on the assumption that \((|G|,|V|)=1\), these character-theoretic estimates are especially relevant when the action is not coprime. They therefore offer potentially useful tools for studying the non-coprime \(k(GV)\)-problem and for identifying the structural features that control the number of conjugacy classes in \(G\ltimes V\).

**Let Irr Remember These**

“Let go,” whispered Irr, though the words felt heavier than the stone in his hand.

Before him stood three doors. One led to the life he had known, another to the future he feared, and the last to everything he had once believed impossible.

“These choices do not define you,” said the old guardian. “What matters is the courage with which you make them.”

Irr opened his fingers and let the stone fall. Its echo faded into the darkness as he stepped toward the third door. For the first time, he understood: letting go was not the end of his journey, but its beginning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise abstract for a research paper on upper bounds for subsets of \(\Irr(GV)\) related to restrictions to cyclic subgroups generated by elements of \(V\), and mention the non-coprime \(k(GV)\)-problem.
counterfactuals.output: Let \(G\) be a finite group acting on a finite module \(V\), and let \(GV=G\ltimes V\). We establish upper bounds for natural subsets of \(\Irr(GV)\) determined by the restrictions of irreducible characters to cyclic subgroups \(\langle v\rangle\), with \(v\in V\). Our estimates relate character-theoretic data to the orbit and stabilizer structure of the action of \(G\) on \(V\), without assuming that \((|G|,|V|)=1\). As an application, we obtain new reductions and partial bounds relevant to the non-coprime \(k(GV)\)-problem.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Let \(G\) be a finite group and \(V\) a finite \(G\)-module. Draft a brief mathematical summary describing results that bound the number of irreducible characters \(\chi\in\Irr(GV)\) whose restriction to \(\langle v\rangle\), for fixed \(v\in V\), is not a multiple of the regular character.
counterfactuals.output:
Let \(X=G\ltimes V\), where \(V\) is written additively, and fix \(0\neq v\in V\). Put \(A=\langle v\rangle\) and \(n=|A|\). For \(\chi\in\Irr(X)\), write
\[
\chi{\downarrow_A}=\sum_{\lambda\in\Irr(A)}m_{\chi,\lambda}\lambda .
\]
Then \(\chi{\downarrow_A}\) is a multiple of the regular character \(\rho_A\) precisely when all multiplicities \(m_{\chi,\lambda}\) are equal. By Fourier orthogonality,
\[
\sum_{1\neq a\in A}|\chi(a)|^2
   =n\sum_{\lambda\in\Irr(A)}m_{\chi,\lambda}^{\,2}-\chi(1)^2.
\]
Thus this quantity is zero exactly for the characters whose restriction is a multiple of \(\rho_A\). If the restriction is not such a multiple, the quantity is at least \(n-1\). Summing over \(\Irr(X)\) and using column orthogonality gives
\[
(n-1)\,\#\{\chi\in\Irr(X):\chi{\downarrow_A}\notin\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\rho_A\}
 \leq \sum_{1\neq a\in A}|C_X(a)|.
\]
Since \(V\) is abelian,
\[
|C_X(a)|=|V|\,|C_G(a)|,
\]
and hence
\[
\#\{\chi:\chi{\downarrow_A}\text{ is not regular-multiple}\}
\leq
\frac{|V|}{n-1}\sum_{1\neq a\in A}|C_G(a)|.
\]

In the usual case where \(V\) is an elementary abelian \(p\)-group, every nonzero \(v\) has order \(p\), and \(C_G(v^i)=C_G(v)\) for \(1\le i<p\). The bound therefore simplifies to
\[
\#\{\chi\in\Irr(GV):\chi{\downarrow_{\langle v\rangle}}
\text{ is not a multiple of }\rho_{\langle v\rangle}\}
\le |V|\,|C_G(v)|
=|C_{GV}(v)|.
\]
A slightly sharper weighted version is obtained by replacing \(n-1\) with the degree-dependent minimum \(r(n-r)\), where \(r\equiv\chi(1)\pmod n\); if \(r=0\) and the restriction is exceptional, the minimum is \(2n\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a one-paragraph abstract for a finite group theory paper about character-theoretic bounds in the semidirect product \(GV\), emphasizing possible applications to the non-coprime \(k(GV)\)-problem.
counterfactuals.output: Let \(G\) be a finite group acting faithfully on a finite abelian group \(V\), and write \(GV=G\ltimes V\) for the associated semidirect product, without assuming that \((|G|,|V|)=1\). We develop character-theoretic bounds for \(GV\) by combining Clifford theory with orbit–stabilizer analysis of the action of \(G\) on \(\operatorname{Irr}(V)\). In particular, we relate \(k(GV)\), the number of conjugacy classes of \(GV\), to the class numbers and character degrees of inertia subgroups arising from \(G\)-orbits on \(\operatorname{Irr}(V)\), and derive estimates that remain effective in the presence of non-coprime action and nontrivial extension obstructions. These results provide reductions to suitable local subgroups and orbit configurations, offering a framework for investigating non-coprime analogues of the \(k(GV)\)-problem and for identifying structural conditions under which linear bounds for \(k(GV)\) can be obtained.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
